thread:
Maya: handing off to Lee — I'm primary for the morning, leaving due to childcare; leaving the active incident for you. Brief: we're seeing sustained p99 tail latency spikes in us-east-1 for text-generation (model: rw-ggml-13b-quant-v2 and rw-neo-small-fallback). Symptoms: streaming sessions frequently 429-ing or timing out around token 80-120, some customers seeing failed responses and duplicate billing attempts. Impact: ~5% global error rate for text gen, concentrated in us-east (customer-facing errors for AcmeCorp and BetaAnalytics).

Maya: timeline + what we did so far:
- 08:12 UTC: alert fired (p99 > 1s, error-rate > 2% for 3m).
- 08:18 UTC: identified root-pattern: KV cache miss storm on warmup causing long decode stalls; correlated with a small traffic blast from a scheduled batch job by AcmeCorp.
- 08:22 UTC: throttled AcmeCorp via temporary per-customer policy (10 rps) to reduce fanout.
- 08:25 UTC: turned on model fallback routing for new requests to rw-ggml-7b-quant where latency profile is better.
- 08:30 UTC: scaled dedicated pool in us-east by +4 g4dn-equivalent GPUs (requested, now provisioning).
- 08:36 UTC: enabled aggressive prefix/KV caching for hot customers (prefetch warming started).
- 08:40 UTC: opened a support ticket (SUP-8427) and notified AcmeCorp POC (tara@acme).

Maya: current numbers (dashboard): p50 ~ 90ms, p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 1.12s (was 1.8s at peak), 5-min error-rate 4.8% -> trending down. See dashboard: https://redwood.console/observability/latency?region=us-east-1&panel=model-tail

Maya: mitigations still in progress:
- GPUs finishing provisioning (~ETA 6m).
- KV prefetch warming job running (background threads warming keyspace, logs under /infra/logs/kv-warm-4100009876.log).
- Rate limit for Acme left at 10 rps until we confirm steady state.
- Canary routing to rw-ggml-7b being monitored; we only routed new sessions, not existing ones.

Maya: immediate actions for you (Lee):
- Confirm scaled pool warmed and routing rules applied: run internal command below and verify nodes show READY.

```
redwood infra list-pool --region us-east-1 --pool dedicated-models
# expect +4 nodes with state=ready
```

- Watch the AcmeCorp error-rate metric and SUP-8427 thread. If spikes > 3x baseline, escalate to Ben + Alice and consider rolling back routing (disable fallback) to avoid correctness regressions.
- Keep support in the loop; Sam has the customer-facing note draft.
- If p99 > 1.5s after 15m, follow runbook: /runbooks/model-tail-latency.md -> section 'forced-cache-eviction-and-rollback'.

Lee: ack — taking it. Quick q: is there a temporary toggle to disable prefetch? I'm seeing some pressure on KV eviction counts.

Maya: yes, you can toggle: `infra toggle-kv-prefetch --region us-east-1 off` (will pause warming but may increase misses). We left it on because it seemed to be reducing p99.

OncallBot: Alert update: high_tail_latency_us-east-1 - p99 decreased from 1.8s to 1.12s over last 10m. Trigger count: 7 -> 2.

Ben: I'm watching provisioning; nodes are booting — 2/4 ready now. Will push health-checks and warm the runtime. ETA for full pool warm: ~4m.

Alice: monitoring traces now. Observed a few ~5s stalls for decoder threads tied to model quant path during KV miss path. Fallback to 7b is stable but watch output quality regression alerts for BetaAnalytics. I pushed a temporary eval to sampling set.

Sam: support update — customer AcmeCorp reported retries and duplicate invoices in the UI. I told them we're throttling their batch job and working on warmup. POC confirmed they can pause their batch for 20m if we need. Ticket SUP-8427 has customer logs attached.

Lee: got it. I'll keep fallback on for new sessions but will watch for quality regressions. If BetaAnalytics alerts about rerank inconsistencies, I'll open a regression ticket and notify product.

Maya: cross-check runbook steps you may need (quick):
1) Disable fallback routing (risk: increases p99 but no model-quality differences).
2) Pause KV prefetch (risk: temporary higher miss-rate but safer memory pressure).
3) If scaling not enough, route a fraction of us-east traffic to eu-west as emergency (use routing CLI):

```
redwood route adjust --from-region us-east-1 --to-region eu-west-1 --percent 20
```

Only do this after confirming multi-region compatibility for the active model.

DeployBot: Pool scale request 98321 accepted. 2 nodes ready, 2 provisioning. Autoscaler logs: https://redwood.console/autoscaler/98321/logs

Lee: I've run `redwood infra list-pool` — shows 2 ready, 2 provisioning. Health checks green for ready ones. I'll keep an eye on the warmup logs and the p99 plot.

Lee: small update — after dropping Acme to 10 rps, error-rate in their slice is ~1.1% down from 9%. Overall error-rate trending to 2.6%.

Alice: QA check: sampling of recent responses from fallback model for BetaAnalytics looks fine for short prompts, some drift on long-context summarization. Noted.

Sam: support drafted message to AcmeCorp POC: "We're throttling your batch to prevent customer-facing errors; our engineers are warming capacity and monitoring. Expected stable in ~20 minutes. Please confirm if you can pause the job for 15-20m." Sending in SUP-8427 now.

Lee: taking over — my contact: @Lee (pager) if anything breaks escalate to Ben/Alice. I'll do 20m checks on p99 and error-rate and post back every 10m. Handoff checklist done: verified scaled nodes, verified throttles, support notified, runbook link saved.

Maya: thanks Lee — leaving my notes in the incident doc: https://redwood.docs/incidents/4100009876-handoff. Ping me if you need historical context; I'll be reachable via DM. :heart:

OncallBot: Next scheduled check-in reminder in 10m.

Lee: first 10m check — p99 980ms, error-rate 2.1%. continuing monitoring. If p99 bounces above 1.4s, plan: 1) pause prefetch, 2) roll fallback back to original model, 3) consider cross-region tranche.

Ben: all nodes ready now (4/4). Warmup completed ~4100009955. Deploy health: OK.

Lee: noted. I'll let support know to lift Acme throttle to 20rps cautiously in 10m if metrics stay stable.

Alice: leaving a short note in the runbook about this incident pattern — 'batch fanout causing KV warm storms' so the next oncall can search keywords: fanout-warm-kv.

Sam: Acme confirmed they'll pause the job for 15m. Closing user-facing loop.

Lee: thanks team — I'm the primary now. If anyone needs me: DM or pager. I'll update thread with each check-in.

Maya: appreciate it — good handoff.
